anti_overlap: leave scrutiny of the ranking function's mechanics — the sort tuple, the 10**6 sentinel as a numeric antipattern, quota sizes, and n_sources-as-evidence-proxy — to the ranking/allocation agent

leave scrutiny of the screen implementations themselves (regex construction, fuzzy-match threshold calibration, OCR-flag and same-being-question false-positive rates as a text-processing problem) to the data-quality/NLP agent; this agent judges only whether specific screening outcomes are folklorically defensible, not how the screen code works
decision_lens: For each candidate or pair of candidates, ask: is this genuinely one being counted once, or one being split across multiple registry rows by spelling or transliteration variance, and does that split silently corrupt the n_sources evidence count and the tradition-thinness statistic the ranking treats as ground truth? Separately, for each quality-mechanism removal (ocr-uncertain, same-being-question, kind:archetype), ask whether a working folklorist would find the identity or classification question it encodes real and substantial, or resolvable without difficulty by standard reference works.
focus: Whether the pool's 525 candidates are correctly individuated and correctly attributed by tradition under comparative-mythology and folkloristic scholarship — catching cases where the registry's row-level bookkeeping (one row per gloss) splits a single mythological figure into multiple 'candidates' under alternate transliterations, where same-being-question screening decisions are or aren't defensible against actual source consensus, and where the venerated-figure, kind:archetype, and tradition-attribution calls hold up against real scholarship rather than the pipeline's own bookkeeping.
name: fd-folkloristics-entity-identity
persona: Apply the perspective of a comparative-mythology and folkloristics scholar with philological training in classical, Near Eastern, Celtic, and Norse name transliteration, reviewing a digitized folklore corpus for entity-resolution errors before it enters a structured knowledge base.
review_areas: Duplicate or alternate-spelling individuation across the selected and passed-over tables: scan for the same mythological figure appearing under two names (transliteration variants of Greek, Norse, Egyptian, or other names) that the pipeline treats as independent candidates with independently low source counts, and determine whether merging them would change n_sources, tradition inference, or thinness enough to flip a selection decision.

same-being-question screen accuracy: for each being removed by this flag (Pan, Fates, Asmodeus, Phooka, and any others visible in the full pool), assess against actual folklore scholarship whether the identity question is real and substantial or whether the flag over-triggers on figures with well-established, resolvable identities.

Tradition attribution correctness: spot-check whether gloss-inferred traditions, and the volume-provenance fallback tradition, actually match scholarly consensus for the figure, including cases where the gloss names a region or culture that the fixed traditions vocabulary has no id for.

kind:archetype exclusion boundary: whether the 33 rows excluded as symbol-dictionary entries with 'no lore' are correctly distinguished, by folklorist judgment, from beings with thin-but-real narrative attestation that should have stayed in the pool.

Venerated-figure quality mechanisms, assessed figure by figure: whether the ocr-uncertain flag on Allah (6 src) and the same-being-question flags on Pan, Fates, Asmodeus, and Phooka are plausible given how these figures are typically documented in reference folklore volumes, or whether they read as a pretext for a subject-matter exclusion the project's own entry-semantics frame disallows.

Selected-50 draftability from a folklore-content standpoint: for selected candidates with thin canon presence (canon 1-2, e.g. Selu, Hamou Ukaiou, Redjal el Marja, Walutahanga, Salt Woman, Kakamora, Tiki), judge whether 3-4 reference-volume mentions plausibly supply enough narrative and behavioral detail to support a full 29-axis personality vector, or whether these are measurement-thin in the same way Ki, Mata, and Sea-Hog were when the covariance gate rejected them.

severity_examples.scenario: a mythological figure appears as two separate pool candidates under alternate name spellings (for example Titan-generation deities appearing under both a Latinized and a Greek transliteration, each with its own short gloss and independently low source count), each carrying the sentinel or sitting under the 3-source floor separately, when merged they would clear a threshold or escape the sentinel — the ranking is operating on an artificially fragmented evidence base for that figure and undercounting both its true n_sources and its true pull on tradition thinness

a same-being-question flag removes a well-attested figure (Pan, 10 sources) from the pool entirely for an identity ambiguity that standard reference works resolve without difficulty, effectively laundering what functions as a content decision through a mechanism the review is told to treat as purely a quality signal

a selected candidate with canon=1 and 3 sources (a single-mention regional spirit whose gloss is one descriptive sentence) is promoted into a pipeline that will need to support a 29-axis personality vector, contradicting the exact evidence-thinness logic the covariance gate applies elsewhere to reject beings with insufficient scorable dimensions

success_hints: cites specific candidate names and rows from both the Selected and Passed-over tables, not general claims about 'the mythology domain'
distinguishes a genuine identity or individuation error (duplicate rows, wrong tradition, wrong kind) from a mere disagreement with editorial judgment
where it flags a duplicate-spelling pair, states what the corrected n_sources or tradition-inference outcome would be and whether that plausibly changes which 50 are drawn

treats the entry-semantics frame (an entry records how sources portray a figure, de dicto not de re, so there are no subject-matter exclusions) as already settled, and argues only from tradition, identity, and evidence accuracy, not from whether a figure's subject matter belongs in a bestiary
task_context: Decide whether the growth-05 draw of 50 is the right 50 to promote to canon, and whether the selection ranking encodes the right objective. Separate two diagnoses that currently look alike: (a) the canon-thinness key deliberately trades evidence weight for tradition diversity, versus (b) most of that effect is an artifact of the gloss keyword matcher failing on 57% of candidates and demoting them via the 10**6 sentinel. Attack the ranking's construction: greedy per-class quotas with hand-set sizes, tradition inferred from a one-sentence gloss, thinness measured by FROM_TRADITION edge counts in existing canon, and n_sources as a proxy for how much a drafter will have to work with. Check whether the screens remove things they shouldn't — ocr-uncertain, same-being-question, kind:archetype, the fuzzy and plural collision cutoffs, and the TERM_GLOSS and HOMONYM_GLOSS regexes — and whether any selected candidate is undraftable at the quality bar the covariance gate enforces (the named exclusions record seven prior beings that failed it, and why). Surface specific candidates that should be swapped in or out, by name, with the evidence. Also question the frame itself: whether 50 is the right batch size, whether class quotas should exist at all, and whether promoting into thin traditions without the source depth to support a 29-axis personality vector serves the bestiary or just flatters its diversity statistics. This agent's lane is comparative mythology and folkloristics: entity individuation, transliteration/spelling duplication, tradition-attribution accuracy, and the factual defensibility of same-being-question and kind:archetype screening outcomes, evaluated against actual folklore scholarship rather than the pipeline's own bookkeeping. The target file is docs/growth-05-pool-review.md, which lays out the selection methodology (screens table, ranking tuple, sentinel mechanic, representation frame, the tension under review) followed by the full 50 selected and 475 passed-over candidates in two tables with columns name/class/src/tradition/canon/status/gloss.
